limitations: Candidate binding does not adopt or activate the workflow
Schema conformance does not prove runtime or Product outcome conformance

claim_ceiling: Illustrative cross-linked candidate records only; no record is admitted or adopted and no realization or value claim is established.

product.claim_ceiling: Candidate Product Identity/v2 fixture only. It does not admit Craft, commit its thesis, adopt a Capability, prove value, or authorize implementation or runtime effects.
product.name: Craft
product.purpose: Provide a governed recursive system-building Product while preserving its identity separately from Projects, methods, theses, Capabilities, contexts, repositories, and implementations.

includes: Craft Product meaning and value boundary
Same-Product lineage continuity from DomainSpec v2

product.value_promise: Help people and machine collaborators understand, change, and validate complex systems while keeping meaning, evidence, ownership, authority, and unresolved residue explicit.

acceptance_conditions: Every admitted Definition version is bound by exact path and digest
The canonical registry and human index agree on admitted current versions
Admission does not activate downstream consumers
product_capability.name: Governed Definition Admission
product_capability.outcome: Repository owners can admit exact semantic Definitions while preserving provenance, review authority, drift visibility, and separation from consumer activation.

assumptions: Repository work benefits from explicit semantic and authority boundaries
Machine assistance is more useful when claims remain tied to evidence
Human owners must retain admission and effect authority
product_thesis.audience: Repository owners and human-machine engineering teams building governed software systems
boundaries: The thesis does not prove that Craft is implemented or effective
One Project or experiment cannot prove the complete thesis
The thesis does not authorize deployment, publication, or external effects
first_order_principles: Human owners retain consequential decision authority
Incomplete or unsupported claims remain visible residue
Product identity remains separate from projects and implementations
Realizations remain replaceable behind governed contracts

hypotheses.statement: Explicit semantic and authority boundaries improve decision clarity enough to justify their maintenance cost.
Evidence-bound machine collaboration preserves human agency better than unconstrained automation.

intended_outcomes.statement: People can identify the current authoritative meaning and decision state.
Machine collaborators can operate within explicit evidence and authority boundaries.
Projects can evolve without silently redefining the Product.

product_thesis.problem: Repository knowledge, decisions, evidence, and implementation work become fragmented across documents and tools, making authority and current state difficult to establish.
revision_criteria: Evidence shows the governed workflow adds more burden than decision clarity
Users cannot determine which artifacts or decisions are authoritative
A simpler model provides equivalent traceability and authority separation
product_thesis.value_mechanism: Typed artifacts, exact provenance, explicit owner decisions, bounded evidence, and replaceable implementations keep meaning and authority inspectable while work evolves.
product_thesis.value_proposition: Craft provides a governed human-machine work loop that preserves intent, shared meaning, evidence, ownership, bounded authority, and visible incompleteness.
